lesson.title: Ratio vs rate vs unit rate
lesson.html: A ratio compares quantities. A rate compares different units. A unit rate has 1 in the denominator.

lesson.title: Cross-multiplication in 4 steps
lesson.html: 1) Unit template (answer units on top). 2) Standard proportion. 3) Variable proportion. 4) Cross-multiply and solve.

lesson.title: Formulas
lesson.html:
% of change: (new − old) ÷ old = x/100.
Simple interest: I = P · R · T (R in decimal form).

pairs: Ratio
A way to compare two or more quantities; it can be written like a fraction
Rate
A quantity measured per unit of something else
Proportion
An equation in which two ratios, rates or fractions are set equal
Ratio Table
A structured list of equivalent ratios
Scale Factor
The number that tells how much a ratio is enlarged or shrunk
Unit Rate
A ratio between two quantities where the denominator is 1
Complex Fraction
A number written as a fraction that contains other fractions
Equivalent
Equal; mathematical objects that can replace each other even if the symbols look different
Additive Relationship
A relationship involving addition: something that happens once
Multiplicative Relationship
A relationship involving multiplication: something that happens the same way repeatedly

list.q: Why is using a scale factor the same as expanding or simplifying a fraction?
list.a: They're the same thing with different names
w: Scale factors only work with decimals
list.why: Ratios and rates are fractions and follow the same rules.

list.q: Why are all proportional relationships multiplicative?
list.a: Proportions are equivalent fractions made by multiplying or dividing by a form of one
w: They are made by adding the same number

list.a: Decide the unit template (what units the answer is in)
list.why: The focus (answer units) goes in the numerator.

list.q: How do you compare two ratios?
list.a: Multiply each numerator by the other fraction's denominator
list.why: Expand to a common denominator and compare numerators.
